questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The new bride is going to be admired by everyone in the family.
options_en: Everybody in the family is going to admire the new bride.
Everybody in the family was admiring the new bride.
Everybody in the family has been going to admire the new bride.
Everybody in the family was going to admire the new bride.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

In Active voice, the sentence should be in the Infinitive form (to + V1).

The format in Passive voice is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are/was/were + going+ to + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format in Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are/was/were + going + to + V1 + Object.

For example:

She is going to be helped by you. (Passive)

You are going to help her. (Active)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Professionalism is probably the _____ (A) theoretical of the types of soft skills, and certainly the most dependent on context. What professionalism ______ (B) in one organization can be very different from what it means in another. In general, what most employers mean when they say they are _______ (C) for professionalism is someone who understands how they as an individual affect the ______ (D) as a whole. Select the appropriate word to fill blank D.
questions.solution_en:
The blank requires a noun to denote the thing that is affected by individuals in the context of an organization. Since there is no such adjective before the blank, these options are generic and thus negated. 'Day' is the same as the previous two options, a more generic option and requires an adjective to explain its relevance to the sentence, so it is also negated. 'Work' (activity involving mental or physical effort done in order to achieve a purpose or result) denotes the thing that is affected by a person's professionalism.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

Qualifiers: A word or phrase that limits the meaning of another word or phrase or makes it less general. 'Adverbs' and 'adjectives' are qualifiers.

When the escaped convict (were apprehended by the authorities), he was hiding in an abandoned warehouse.

Therefore, the correct form of the verb should also be in the past tense. 'Was apprehended' is the correct past tense form of the verb 'apprehend' for the third-person singular subject 'the escaped convict'. The other options do not provide the correct verb form or subject-verb agreement. Option (b) uses the present tense 'is apprehended' instead of the correct past tense 'was apprehended'. Option (c) does not use the correct past tense form of the verb 'apprehend'. Option (d) uses the present tense 'are apprehended' instead of the correct past tense 'was apprehended'. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or both plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb.

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The employees felt pressured to meet the tight deadlines set by the demanding project manager during the quarter.
options_en: The employees may feel pressured to meet the tight deadlines set by the demanding project manager during the quarter.
The demanding project manager was setting tight deadlines, pressuring the employees to meet them during the quarter.
The demanding project manager set the tight deadlines, pressuring the employees to meet them during the quarter.
The employees feeling pressured to meet the tight deadlines set by the demanding project manager during the quarter.
questions.solution_en:
In the original sentence, the focus is on the employees who "felt pressured." Option (c) transforms the sentence into active voice by making the demanding project manager the subject of the sentence, highlighting their actions.

Subject: "The demanding project manager" - This is the doer of the action in the sentence. In the active voice, the subject typically performs the action.

Verb: "set" - This is an action verb indicating what the demanding project manager did. The verb is active and clearly states the manager's role in the situation.

Since the sentence in passive voice is in past simple tense, the sentence in active voice should also be in the past simple tense. That's why option (b) with the verb form 'was setting' [past continuous] is incorrect.

Object: "the tight deadlines" - This is what the demanding project manager set. It is the direct object of the verb "set."

Complement: "pressuring the employees to meet them during the quarter" - This part of the sentence describes the impact of the manager's action. It explains how the set deadlines are pressuring the employees and emphasizes the cause-and-effect relationship.

Option (c) successfully transforms the original sentence from passive voice to active voice by placing the focus on the demanding project manager and clearly stating their actions. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that will improve the boldened part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

The traffic constable given instructions to us.
questions.solution_en:
In the phrase given in bold, the past participle verb 'given' can be used only if it is used in a perfect tense sentence (has/have/had + verb (past participle form). In option (b), the plural verb 'have' is grammatically not suitable because the noun 'traffic constable' is singular, so the option is negated. In option (c), the base form of the verb 'give' is suggested instead of a past participle verb, so it is also negated. Option (d), 'has given instructions' is the only option that is grammatically and contextually correct to replace the incorrect phrase in the sentence.

The correct sentence is: The traffic constable has given instructions to us.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an INCORRECT preposition.

Please remember to take / your notice to the reception area / if you want it to be displayed / upon the bulletin board.
options_en: if you want it to be displayed
your notice to the reception area
questions.solution_en:
Let's analyze each segment for the use of prepositions:

· Option 1: "Please remember to take" - This segment has no preposition, just the verb "take." It's grammatically correct as part of the sentence.

· Option 2: "upon the bulletin board" - The preposition "upon" is incorrect here. The standard preposition for displaying something on a bulletin board is "on," not "upon." "Upon" is more formal and typically used in different contexts (e.g., "upon arrival"). The correct phrase should be "on the bulletin board."

· Option 3: "if you want it to be displayed" - This segment has no preposition and is grammatically correct as a conditional clause.

· Option 4: "your notice to the reception area" - The preposition "to" is correct here, indicating the destination of the notice (i.e., "take your notice to the reception area").

The incorrect preposition is in Option 2, where "upon" should be replaced with "on."

Thus, the format in Passive voice will be: Let + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + be + V3.

For example:

Start the match. (Active)

Let the match be started. (Passive)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): Let the access be denied.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. However, the rapid growth of urban areas has led to challenges such as housing shortages, traffic congestion, pollution, and the strain on public services, raising questions about the sustainability of this expansion.

B. As urbanization continues to accelerate, city planners and governments must find innovative solutions to create smart, sustainable urban environments that can accommodate growing populations while preserving natural resources.

C. Urbanization, the movement of people from rural areas to cities, has become one of the defining trends of the modern era, reshaping economies, social structures, and environmental conditions around the world.

D. With cities offering more employment opportunities, better infrastructure, and access to education and healthcare, they have become magnets for populations seeking to improve their quality of life.
questions.solution_en:
• If the sentences are read carefully, it can be noted that the sentences talk about 'urbanization'.

• Sentence C has to come first, as it introduces the central topic that is discussed in the remaining sentences.

• It is followed by the sentence pair DA, which talks about the effect of urbanization in city areas and city planning activities and the straining effects of rapid urbanization.

• Sentence B concludes the discussion by suggesting possible solutions that can mitigate the effects of urbanization. So, the final order is CDAB.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the past tense form.

He will study diligently for the final History exam.
options_en: He studies diligently for the final History exam.
He is studying diligently for the final History exam.
He will be studying diligently for the final History exam.
He had studied diligently for the final History exam.
questions.solution_en:
The verb "will study" is in the future tense. To change it to the past tense, we need to consider the appropriate past tense form. Option (d) correctly changes the future tense "will study" to the past perfect tense "had studied." The past perfect tense is formed by using "had" + the past participle of the verb. In this case, the past participle of "study" is "studied." Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

Note: Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate homonyms from the given alternatives to fill in the blanks.

I didn't ______ to be ______ when I said that.

A. mean (average)

B. mean (verb)

C. mean (cruel)
questions.solution_en:
Mean (verb) is appropriate in the first blank as it refers to the act of conveying an idea or intention: "I didn't mean to be..."

Mean (cruel) fits the context when placed in second blank as it refers to being unkind: "to be mean when I said that."

The words in their respective places give the meaning that the speaker didn't intend to be unkind.

Mean (average) does not fit the context of the sentence, as it relates to a statistical concept.

The correct sentence is: I didn't mean to be mean when I said that.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.
